html:
Atal Bihari Vajpayee was prime minister of India from 1998 to 2004, and briefly in 1996. He was the first prime minister from outside the Congress tradition to serve a full term.

He was born in 1924 in Gwalior, a schoolteacher's son, and joined the RSS as a student. He entered Parliament in 1957 and sat there for almost fifty years. Nehru, hearing him speak, is said to have predicted he would lead the country. He was jailed during the Emergency, served as foreign minister afterwards, and in 1980 became the first president of the BJP.

He was a poet and the best Hindi orator of his time, and he was liked by opponents. That let him hold together a coalition of more than twenty parties.

His years in office:

  • 1998: the nuclear tests at Pokhran.
  • 1999: he rode a bus to Lahore to make peace with Pakistan. The Kargil War followed within months. He tried again in 2001 and 2004.
  • 2001: the Golden Quadrilateral highways and a plan for village roads.
  • Telephones and state firms were opened to private owners.

He told Narendra Modi after the 2002 riots to do his duty as a ruler, and left him in office. He lost the 2004 election and died in 2018.
sum: Atal Bihari Vajpayee was prime minister of India from 1998 to 2004, and briefly in 1996. He was the first prime minister from outside the Congress tradition to serve a full term.
